This second compound is predicted to interact with Mcl-1, a protein involved in cell survival and proliferation, particularly in myeloid leukemia. The presence of a final score of 0.6007 indicates a moderate level of confidence in the predicted interaction, suggesting that Cochinchinenone may modulate Mcl-1 through the intermediacy of the mentioned compounds. The evidence highlights a possible pathway where Cochinchinenone could influence Mcl-1 activity, potentially affecting cell survival and contributing to the regulation of myeloid leukemia progression. The relationship is supported by a chain of molecular interactions, though the exact mechanism remains to be elucidated.
